theorem_title: Actual polynomial order at every pole
formal_statement:

theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalPolynomialOrderAtPole {N : ℕ} (M : Model N)
    (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M) (ψ : M.K) (hψ : Transcendental ℚ ψ)
    (P : Place M.K) (h : ψ ∉ P.1) {p : ℚ[X]} (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    letI : IsCurveField M.K := M.isCurveField
    P.ord (aeval ψ p) = p.natDegree * P.ord ψ := by
  letI : IsCurveField M.K := M.isCurveField
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
> Theorem 2.5. (Belyi Maps Noncritical at Prescribed Points) Let X be a smooth, proper, connected curve over \overline{\mathbb{Q}} and S,T \subseteq X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) finite sets of \overline{\mathbb{Q}}-rational points such that S \cap T = \emptyset. Then there exists a morphism \phi : X \to \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} such that: (a) \phi is unramified over \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\backslash\{0,1,\infty\}; (b) \phi(S) \subseteq \{0,1,\infty\}; (c) we have \phi(T) \cap \{0,1,\infty\} = \emptyset. Moreover, if X, S, and T are defined over a number field F, then \phi may be taken to be defined over F.

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Theorem 2.5, printed pp. 5–6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalPolynomialOrderAtPole`

Let N∈ℕ and M:Model N. Its field K=M.K is an intermediate field of the algebraic closure of ℚ(t), with u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, and K is finite-dimensional of degree N over ℚ(u). A place P is any proper valuation subring O_P of K containing ℚ; κ(P) is its full residue field and res_P:O_P→κ(P) its actual residue homomorphism. The explicit hypothesis hDVR:PlacesDiscrete M says every O_P is a discrete valuation ring. The model also supplies IsCurveField K, from which the normalized integer order ord_P=P.ord is obtained; its defined value at 0 is ord_P(0)=0. The model order defined using hDVR agrees with P.ord. Assume a model M, discrete places, transcendental ψ, a place P, ψ∉O_P, and nonzero rational polynomial p. Then ord_P(p(ψ)) equals natDegree(p) times ord_P(ψ), with the degree cast to ℤ. The hypothesis is p≠0, not positive degree; in particular nonzero constant polynomials are included. The proof body contains sorry, so this is an OPEN child obligation.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalPolynomialOrderAtPole`
